recall.define: For RISC-V and AArch64 execution ports, define ABI stack extent, public-call alignment, port save set, platform register reservation, argument exhaustion boundary, entry-SP offset, owned port context, resume validity, immediate sign reconstruction, relocation admission range, trap interrupt-enable stack, prior privilege field, supervisor user-data window, permission composition, target runtime closure, port evidence boundary, giving each invariant.
recall.distinguish: For RISC-V and AArch64 execution ports, distinguish these near concepts: ABI stack extent versus reserved stack region; public-call alignment versus C object alignment; port save set versus full machine context; platform register reservation versus callee-save convention; argument exhaustion boundary versus source parameter count; entry-SP offset versus frame-local offset; owned port context versus serialized register bytes; resume validity versus numeric address validity; immediate sign reconstruction versus signed C shift; relocation admission range versus linker success; trap interrupt-enable stack versus call save set; prior privilege field versus current execution mode; supervisor user-data window versus supervisor user execution; permission composition versus pointer validity; target runtime closure versus freestanding flag; port evidence boundary versus cross compilation.
recall.apply: Reuse ports.context for coroutine/task adapters; an ABI-preserving call switch, an interrupt frame and a process context must remain separately specified.
